mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month, sustained for two months, signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during such PAYEMS accelerations.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 1.5% and a decline in RSAFS (consumer savings) below the 10th percentile over the prior year jointly signal a deflationary environment with constrained demand, which historically precedes equity market weakness over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% AND RSAFS < 10th percentile for 12 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the prior 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prior 12-month mean +10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such HOUST recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for four consecutive months after a prior tightening cycle, market expectations of prolonged low rates support risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for 4 consecutive months after a tightening cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such post-tightening plateaus.
